Subject: Architecture constraints: decision log + demo request

Hi Marta,

Thanks again for carving out time today — quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum.

Call highlights (short):
- Nimbus priority: tight p99 latency for your conversational agents and strict tenant isolation for PHI-adjacent workloads.
- Primary deployment options on the table: Hosted API (multi-tenant), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools), Private VPC (VPC-hosted control plane / on-prem later).
- Your main risks: noisy-neighbor variability at peak, auditability for SLOs, and a preference for deterministic failover behavior.

What we propose next:
1) Evidence pack: we will share an architecture sketch and an anonymized p95/p99 latency breakdown from similar customers (attached).
2) Deep-dive demo: schedule a 60min session with our infra engineer to walkthrough isolation mechanics (GPU isolation, KV cache trimming, eviction behavior) and SLO dashboards.
3) Proof-of-concept scope: minimal PoC with a representative workload (2 concurrent services, 30 req/s peak), duration 2 weeks. We can scope Dedicated vs Hosted based on initial load tests.

As attachments I included a short arch sketch and a sample SLO export: redwood-quick-arch.pdf, slo-metrics-sample.csv.

Asks from you:
- Confirm stakeholders to include on the deep-dive (ops/security/infra).
- Any compliance docs we should prepare in advance (e.g., specific SOC 2 sections, custom retention constraints).

If that looks good, I’ll propose meeting slots later today.

Thanks,
— Soojin

From: Marta Novak <marta@nimbuslabs.com>

Subject: Re: Architecture constraints: decision log + demo request

Thanks, Soojin — helpful recap. A few clarifying items before we pull in the rest of the team: 

1) For Hosted API (multi-tenant) you mentioned automatic prefix/KV caching. How do you guarantee noisy-neighbor risk when a single tenant has a cache-heavy spike? Do you throttle at the request planning layer or evict aggressively?
2) For Dedicated capacity: is there a hard isolation boundary (completely dedicated GPU pools) or are there shared control-plane components that can still cause noisy-neighbor-like symptoms?
3) For Private VPC/on-prem: what parts remain under Redwood control vs our ops team?

Also, our security lead (security@nimbuslabs.com) asked whether we can get anonymized SLO traces that show tail latency during a traffic burst — that will help us model risk.

Please include Marissa from your infra team on the deep-dive if she’s available.

Best,
Marta
Director of Platform, Nimbus Labs

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marta Novak <marta@nimbuslabs.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Architecture constraints: decision log + demo request

Hi Marta — quick technical answers to your three bullets, plus what we’ll cover in the deep-dive.

1) Hosted API (multi-tenant) — noisy neighbor mitigation
- Continuous batching + request shaping: the serving runtime groups requests by model and sequence-length distribution; we apply admission control when queue latency would breach the SLO budget.
- Prefix/KV cache isolation: per-tenant namespaces for KV cache; eviction is LRU within a tenant and global backpressure is applied when aggregate cache memory approaches a configurable threshold. In practice, we have two levers: proactive admission control (preferred) and emergency eviction (last resort).
- QoS limits: token-per-second caps per API key and soft limits that scale with priority tiers (we can adjust for Nimbus).

2) Dedicated capacity — what is actually dedicated
- Compute: dedicated GPU pools are reserved for the tenant; during allocation we pin workloads so they do not share the same GPU instance with other tenants.
- Control plane: management/control-plane services (deployment API, metrics ingestion) are multi-tenant but isolated by tenancy-aware RBAC + per-tenant metrics partitions. Control-plane saturation can be mitigated by throttling metrics ingestion and providing a hot path for critical control messages.
- Blast radius: we provide a documented blast-radius model and an SLA addendum showing the boundaries for Dedicated contracts (we’ll share the addendum draft).

3) Private VPC/on-prem — responsibilities
- Customer-managed network and KMS: network and KMS keys remain in your control.
- Optional on-prem bundle: we install runtime nodes behind your firewall; Redwood provides the control plane or a private control-plane option depending on contract.

SLO traces & artifacts we’ll provide for the deep-dive:
- Anonymized p95/p99 traces during a synthetic 3x load burst (CSV)
- Example isolation playbook: how we escalate and remediate noisy-neighbor events (PDF)
- Dashboard walkthrough (live): latency breakdown by shard, per-key token counters, eviction logs.

Attachments for your review: slo-metrics-sample.csv, isolation-playbook.pdf.

Deep-dive agenda (30–45min):
- 10min: architecture overview and isolation model
- 15min: live dashboard + SLO traces during burst test
- 10min: Q&A + PoC scoping

Proposed slots (PT): Tue 22 Jun 09:00, Tue 22 Jun 15:00, Wed 23 Jun 11:00. Which works for you and your security lead?

— Marissa
